newsitem.title: GERMANY: German feed demand boosted by switch from beef.
newsitem.headline: German feed demand boosted by switch from beef.

text.p: German producers of compound feed reported a 2.6 percent rise in output in January-August as a consumer shift from beef to pork and poultry increased demand, industry data showed.
The FFMI industry association said on Tuesday that Jan-August production, at 12.70 million tonnes, compared with 12.37 million in the same 1995 period.
Production levels reflected consumption quite closely, with little compound feed kept in store.
"Lower beef consumption has boosted poultry and pork sales and this translated back into higher demand for poultry and pig feed," said FFMI managing director Hubert Grote.
"A corresponding decline in beef cattle feed requirements has not seriously hit the industry because some 90 percent of beef feeds are for dairy cows," he added.
Beef cattle slaughterings rose and meat prices dropped sharply this year because of consumer fears over so-called mad cow disease.
Pig feed output in the period under review rose by 4.9 percent to 3.98 million tonnes and poultry feed by 2.5 percent to 2.74 million.
Most of the overall increase was recorded in eastern Germany, where producers raised Jan-August volumes by 7.6 percent to 2.21 million tonnes.
Use of citrus pulp, molasses and wheat/rye germ meal was up, but use of corngluten and pulses fell.
Feed grain use in the eight months was up by 18.8 percent from a year earlier at 670,000 tonnes.
